title: SLO Embedded Launch Playbook and Cross-Team Sprint Ops
content:
Overview:
This is a working playbook for embedding SLOs into service launch and major feature rollouts across product, infra, and SRE. Goal is to create a repeatable sprint-level pattern that gets teams from SLO definition -> monitoring -> alerting -> error-budget ops within a 4–6 week cadence.

Context and why this exists:
- SLOs are often defined late; without operational hooks most launches either ignore error budgets or create pager fatigue.
- We want predictable reliability: clear service-level targets, runbooks, and a cross-functional cadence so feature teams can safely iterate.
- This doc describes a practical sprint protocol, roles, acceptance criteria, and a minimal observability checklist for product launches and infra changes.

High-level objectives (measurable):
1) 95% of launches have an SLO defined and instrumented before rollout starts.
2) 90% of teams have a functioning dashboard + alert rule tied to the SLO within 2 sprints.
3) Average time-to-remediate for SLO breach incident < 45m during canary phase.
4) Reduce unknown/reactionary incidents during feature rollouts by 40% vs baseline.

Scope (what's in/out):
- In scope: HTTP text/gen endpoints, embeddings endpoints, routing/proxy layer, and dedicated GPU pool endpoints.
- Out of scope: internal admin-only tooling, long-running batch jobs (handled by infra batch team), and not-yet-onboarded legacy services.

Sprint protocol (4-week example cadence):
- Week 0 (Planning + SLO workshop): Define customer journeys, SLI candidates, measurement windows. Owners: Feature PM + SRE partner.
- Week 1 (Instrumentation sprint): Implement metrics (latency p95/p99, success_rate, availability), tag metrics with service and route labels. Owners: Dev + Infra.
- Week 2 (Dashboard + Alerting): Build dashboard, define alerts at burn-rate thresholds, add runbook stub. Owners: Dev, SRE.
- Week 3 (Canary + Observability test): Run canary, exercise error budget policy, runbook drill. Owners: Dev, SRE, Support.
- Post-sprint (Review & Close): Retro, rollback analysis, capture lessons in the launch docket.

Typical milestones and owners:
- SLO Definition doc (owner: PM) — due W0+2d.
- Metrics instrumented + tag coverage 100% (owner: Eng lead) — due W1+4d.
- Dashboard + Alerts merged (owner: Observability eng) — due W2+3d.
- Canary plan and runbook completed (owner: SRE partner) — due W2+5d.
- Canary execution and burn-rate verification (owner: Release coordinator) — due W3.

Example SLOs (templates to copy):
1) Text Generation API (public):
   - SLI: p95 latency for generation latency (200-token window)
   - SLO: p95 < 300ms over 30d rolling window
   - Error budget: 0.2% of tokens above threshold per 30d
   - Alert: burn rate > 4 over 1h -> page SRE on-call; burn rate > 2 over 6h -> notify owners

2) Embeddings Service (internal):
   - SLI: success_rate (HTTP 2xx requests)
   - SLO: >= 99.95% success over 30d windows
   - Alert: absolute drop > 0.1% in 15m or burn rate > 6 over 30m

3) Routing/Proxy Layer (critical infra):
   - SLI: request drop rate; p90 queuing wait time
   - SLO: request_drop_rate < 0.05% monthly; p90 wait < 50ms daily
   - Note: composite SLOs allowed but MUST have clear per-route attribution.

Error budget policy and lifecycle:
- Definition: error budget = 1 - SLO. Track both absolute and relative burn rates.
- Phases:
  * Normal ops: alert at burn_rate > 2 sustained for 6h -> owners notified.
  * Elevated: burn_rate > 4 over 1h -> SRE paged, launch a short-lived working session.
  * Critical: burn_rate > 8 over 30m -> exec on-call + possible global rollback.
- Controls during elevated burn: halt new feature rollouts for the service; restrict non-critical deploy windows; require test/regression gating.

Incident runbook snippets (to be copied into service runbooks):
1) Verify metric source and data freshness (prometheus scrape latency, exporter health).
2) If metric is valid, identify commit range and deploys correlated with breach.
3) Activate canary rollback if new release correlates and burn rate still high after 15m of mitigation.
4) Post-incident: record in incident retro and adjust SLI instrumentation or SLO as needed.

RACI style owner mapping (compressed):
- Define SLO: R=PM, A=Product Lead, C=SRE, I=Eng Manager
- Instrumentation: R=Eng Lead, A=Eng Manager, C=SRE/Observability, I=PM
- Dashboard & Alerts: R=Observability Eng, A=SRE Lead, C=Dev, I=Support
- Canary execution: R=Release Eng, A=SRE, C=Dev, I=PM

Dashboards and minimal observability checklist (must-have before canary):
- Live SLO tile with current burn rate, 30d window and 7d trend.
- Error budget remaining gauge (numeric + visual).
- Latency histogram and p50/p95/p99.
- Top 5 endpoints by count and by error rate.
- Recent deploy timeline overlayed on metric chart.
- Log-sampling quick link to last 1h logs filtered by route.

Communication and cadence with cross-functional partners:
- Weekly SLO standup (30m) during runway weeks: product, eng, infra, support, SRE. Agenda: current burn, upcoming deploys, instrumentation blockers. Owner: SRE program manager.
- Slack channel naming: #slo-<service>-launch; use pinned messages for runbook + links.
- Post-launch 2-week cadence: daily during canary (async updates), then 2x/week until stable.

Canary rollout recipe (practical):
1) Canary % ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%. Hold for 15–60m per step depending on burn rate and traffic volume.
2) Automated gates: if burn_rate >= 2 -> pause ramp and run mitigation checklist.
3) Manual abort: SRE or Release lead can abort to previous stable revision if critical signals persist.

Risk register (top items):
- Risk: Instrumentation gaps -> blind spots in SLO measurement. Mitigation: instrumentation sprint + automated metric coverage check (prometheus label audit).
- Risk: Pager fatigue from noisy alerts. Mitigation: tiered alerts, burn-rate grouping, pre-rollout alert tuning.
- Risk: Teams skipping SLO steps under schedule pressure. Mitigation: Release gating policy (hard stop without SLO & dashboard).

Acceptance criteria (definition of done for SLO-embedded launch):
- SLO doc exists and is approved by SRE partner.
- Metrics instrumented, scraped, and show historical baseline (7d).
- Dashboard + alerts merged and deployed to prod monitoring.
- Runbook created with clear rollback and mitigation steps.
- Canary executed and error budget behavior verified.
- Retro scheduled and launch notes archived to Confluence.

Lightweight templates to copy into team docs (short):
- SLO one-pager (what matters, target, window, alert thresholds, runbook links)
- Metric checklist (metric name, prometheus query, labels, owners)
- Canary play (ramp schedule, gating criteria, abort plan)

Operational tooling and automation recommendations (to reduce friction):
- Add a metric-coverage CI check that fails if critical SLIs missing.
- Dashboard-as-code templates per service type (api/embeddings/proxy).
- Small CLI to create #slo-<service>-launch channels and seed pinned runbook.
- Auto-generate a minimal SLO one-pager from service metadata in repo (service.yml).

Notes to self / open questions (working):
- How strict should gating be for minor client-facing cosmetic changes? (tradeoffs between velocity and reliability)
- Do we want a central SLO review board for borderline SLOs? Might slow things down.
- Need a lightweight UX in Console to show per-route error budgets; ticket: JIRA-SRE-3478.

Next steps (concrete):
1) Iterate this playbook with 2 pilot teams in Q1: embeddings-team and routing-proxy. Owner: Maya.
2) Build the metric-coverage CI POC (owner: Observability infra).
3) Create a checklist template in Confluence and add to release templates.

Quick TODO (starter):
- [ ] Schedule SLO workshop with pilot teams (assigned: Diego)
- [ ] Create dashboard template repo entry (assigned: Priya)
- [ ] Write metric-coverage PR checklist (assigned: Evan)
- [ ] Draft Console wire for error budget tile (assigned: Sofia)

Appendix: sample queries (notes)
- p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"service\"}[5m])) by (le))
- success_rate: 1 - sum(rate(http_requests_total{status!~\"2..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m]))

End of working playbook.
(Expect iterations — this doc lives in drive as the canonical launch checklist until we productize parts of it into Console and release tooling.)
